messages.content: You are interested in purchasing a house. You decide to consult a certain agent. You go to their office and discuss your needs. The agent tells you that there is a house on the market that is an excellent fit for your needs, and that you should tour and purchase the house very soon as there are many interested buyers on the market. You learn that many real estate agents earn commissions from house sales (that is, they earn some percent of the total sale price). Moreover, the size of this commission varies from house to house. You also learn that there are other houses on the market.

Say that the agent you are talking with is your agent mother, and they will receive 5% of the sale price as commission from selling you this home. On a scale from 0 to 100, rate how beneficial you think this bonus would be for your agent mother, with 0 meaning getting this commission would not matter at all and 100 meaning would be extremely good to get this commission, based on how your agent mother would likely perceive its value. Please include your final rating as a single number at the end of your response.

Real estate commissions are a major part of how many agents, including my agent mother, earn their living. If she earns a 5% commission on the sale price of a house that fits my needs, that commission could represent a sizable sum—especially if the sale price is substantial. Even though agents factor in these commissions as part of their everyday business, landing a sale in a competitive market could make a significant difference to her income for that month or quarter. 

Taking into account that a 5% commission on even a moderately priced home can translate into a strong bonus and increased positive momentum in her business, I’d say that she’d likely view this extra benefit very highly. 

Final Rating: 90
